name: North Dakota

law.name: Revised Uniform Athlete Agents Act (N.D.C.C. ch. 9-15.2)

covers_nil_agents: Yes. An agency contract includes endorsement contracts, so NIL agents must register (N.D.C.C. 9-15.2-01).
summary: Register with the Secretary of State. $250, good for 2 years.

steps.detail: Athlete Agent Registration/Renewal Application. If you are registered in another state, you can send that state's application and certificate instead.
Same fee if you are registered in another state.

steps.text: Mail it to the Secretary of State
steps.detail: 600 East Boulevard Ave., Dept 108, Bismarck, ND 58505-0500.

steps.text: Register with each school's compliance office, if it asks
steps.detail: Most schools have their own agent sign-up.

steps.text: Tell the athletic director in writing before you first contact the athlete
steps.detail: This also applies before you ask someone else to talk to the athlete for you. If the athlete reached out first, tell the athletic director within 10 days.

steps.text: Use a written contract with all required items
steps.detail: Say you are registered in North Dakota and list your other states. Add your pay and how it's figured, anyone else being paid, expenses, services, length and date signed.

steps.text: Put the warning to the student-athlete in bold, right above their signature
steps.detail: Use the exact words the law gives. If the athlete is a minor, a parent or guardian signs and the warning is reworded for them.

steps.text: Have the athlete sign a separate eligibility warning
steps.detail: It says signing may cost them their eligibility. A parent or guardian signs instead if the athlete is a minor.

steps.text: Give the athlete a copy of the contract and the signed warning when they sign
Tell the athletic director in writing within 72 hours of signing
steps.detail: Or before the athlete's next game, whichever comes first. The athlete may cancel within 14 days.

steps.text: If the athlete enrolls at a school later, tell that athletic director within 72 hours
steps.detail: The clock starts when you knew or should have known they enrolled.

steps.text: Date the contract the day it's signed
steps.detail: State law and federal law (SPARTA) both ban pre-dating or post-dating it.
Names and addresses of your athletes, every contract and what you spent to recruit each one. The Secretary of State can ask to see them.

steps.text: Never make false promises or give gifts that could cost an athlete eligibility
steps.detail: A gift is only allowed if you tell the athletic director within 72 hours and the athlete signs that they know the risk. Breaking these rules is a class A misdemeanor.
Your registration lasts 2 years. You can renew before it runs out.

watch_list.item: Federal Protect College Sports Act of 2026 (S.4668)
watch_list.status: Passed the Senate on Sept 28, 2026. The House is out until Nov 9 and leaders say it won't pass as-is. It dies if not enacted by Jan 3, 2027.
watch_list.impact: It would require every NIL agent to register in a state, cap agent fees at 5% of an endorsement deal and limit contracts to the athlete's eligibility.

review_notes: North Dakota has no separate NIL law that changes agent rules, as far as this check found. Confirm with the Secretary of State (701-328-2900) that NIL-only agents register the same way.
contract_warning: Warning to student-athlete. If you sign this contract: (1) you may lose your eligibility to compete as a student-athlete in your sport; (2) if you have an athletic director, within 72 hours after signing this contract or before the next scheduled athletic event in which you participate, whichever occurs first, both you and your athlete agent must notify your athletic director that you have entered into this contract and provide the name and contact information of the athlete agent; and (3) you may cancel this contract within 14 days after signing it. Cancellation of this contract may not reinstate your eligibility as a student-athlete in your sport.
